sources.entry: Termstead - Native SSH client with a session tree, jump hosts, split panes and SFTP beside the terminal.

summary.one_liner: Termstead is a native macOS SSH, RDP and Telnet client with a session tree, tabs, split panes, SFTP beside the terminal, and passwords stored in the macOS Keychain.
summary.what_it_does: Termstead organizes saved sessions in a tree of groups and subgroups, with pinned favorites, search and keyboard navigation. Each connection runs in a tab and each tab runs the system OpenSSH client, with jump host chains, port forwarding (local, remote and SOCKS) and an SFTP tab that reuses the open connection. The window can be split into two or four panes, and broadcast input can send typing to all visible panes. It also offers a local Mac terminal tab, snippets, per-session text logs, automatic reconnection after network drops, and RDP remote desktops in tabs via FreeRDP. Passwords and key passphrases are stored in the login Keychain, and the app can import hosts from ~/.ssh/config.
use_cases: manage many SSH servers from one Mac app
connect to servers through jump hosts
browse and transfer files to remote servers with SFTP
open Windows remote desktops (RDP) alongside SSH tabs
run the same command across several servers at once
tunnel traffic with SSH port forwarding
connect to network switches and routers over Telnet
how_to_run: Or download Termstead.dmg from Releases, open it and drag Termstead to Applications
Build from source: brew install xcodegen cmake ninja
scripts/build-rdp-deps.sh # FreeRDP and OpenSSL for the RDP engine, once
xcodebuild -project Termstead.xcodeproj -scheme Termstead -configuration Release -derivedDataPath build build
notable: Runs the system OpenSSH client rather than its own SSH code, so agent, ssh config, known_hosts and ProxyJump work as in Terminal
RDP desktops are drawn by FreeRDP in a separate process so a crash does not take down Termstead
Broadcast input across split panes with per-pane opt-out
SFTP follows the terminal's current folder and reuses the open connection
Session settings and snippets stored as JSON under Application Support
caveats: Telnet is unencrypted, as the README itself warns
Building from source needs a separate FreeRDP and OpenSSL build step before the Xcode build
